text:
Pipedash 
 One dashboard for CI/CD pipelines across multiple providers. 
 Website Live Demo Downloads Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 Features

 
 
 
 Monitor 
 See the status of every pipeline in one place, or in a build monitor like CCMenu or Nevergreen through the web server's feed. 
 Dashboard Provider health 
 
 
 Organize 
 Group pipelines into saved views with rules, pins and bulk actions. 
 Views 
 
 
 Investigate 
 Find out why a run failed and rerun one GitHub Actions job from its log. 
 Run logs Metrics 
 
 
 Act 
 Start a workflow with inputs or cancel active runs in batches. 
 Trigger and cancel 
 
 
 Notify 
 Get an alert when a pipeline fails, recovers, a run sits in the queue too long or the pipeline stops running on its usual schedule. 
 Notifications 
 
 
 

 About

Pipedash shows pipelines from the supported CI/CD providers in one table, so finding a failed build no longer means switching between dashboards. It polls each provider with a token or kubeconfig and caches the results. The same table opens, triggers, reruns and cancels runs.

It runs as a desktop app, as a self-hosted web server in Docker or as an iOS and Android app. All of them share one Rust core.

 Supported providers

 
 
 
 GitHub Actions 
 GitLab CI 
 Gitea Actions 
 Bitbucket Pipelines 
 Azure DevOps 
 
 
 CircleCI 
 Buildkite 
 Jenkins 
 Woodpecker CI 
 Tekton CD 
 
 
 ArgoCD 
 FluxCD 
 Prow 
 Komodo 
 Coolify 
 
 
 Argo Workflows 
 
 
 

 Get started

- Install it with the installation guide.
- Add a provider with the quick start.
- Run it on desktop, mobile or Docker.
- Share one server through Server mode, a reverse proxy or the REST API.
- Configure settings, tokens and the cache, or move providers and run history between storage backends.
- Keep providers in a file : each block in config.toml adds a provider, and deleting the block removes it.

 Contributing

- Contribute through the contribution guide and GitHub issues.
- Build locally with the development guide. Run mise install first.
- Write a plugin for a new provider with plugin development.
- Learn the architecture and the security model.
- Get help from support.
